verses.38:22: And I will judge him with death and blood and flooding rain and hailstones, and I will rain fire and sulfur upon him and upon all those with him and upon many nations with him.
verses.38:23: And I will be magnified and sanctified and glorified and made known before many nations, and they will know that I am the Lord.'"
verses.39:1: "And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, 'Thus says the Lord: Look, I am against you, Gog, ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.
verses.39:2: And I will gather you and guide you and bring you up at the farthest north, and I will bring you up onto the mountains of Israel.
verses.39:3: And I will destroy your bow from your left hand and your arrows from your right hand, and I will cast you down upon the mountains of Israel,
verses.39:4: and you will fall, you and all those around you, and the nations with you will be given to multitudes of birds; to every winged creature and to all the wild beasts of the field I have given you to be devoured.
verses.39:5: Upon the face of the field you will fall, for I have spoken, says the Lord.
verses.39:6: And I will send fire upon Gog, and the islands will be inhabited in peace, and they will know that I am the Lord.
verses.39:7: And My holy name will be made known in the midst of My people Israel, and My holy name will no longer be profaned; and the nations will know that I am the Lord, holy in Israel.
verses.39:8: Look, it has come, and you will know that it will be, says the Lord, the Lord; this is the day on which I spoke.
verses.39:9: And those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out and burn the weapons—shields and pikes and bows and arrows and hand staffs and spears—and they will burn fire with them for seven years;
verses.39:10: and they will by no means take wood from the field nor cut from the forests, but rather they will burn up the weapons with fire; and they will plunder those who plundered them, and they will despoil those who despoiled them, says the Lord.
verses.39:11: And it will be in that day that I will give Gog a renowned place, a tomb in Israel, the burial ground of those who approached by the sea, and they will build a wall around the mouth of the ravine;
verses.39:12: and they will bury Gog there and all his multitude, and it will be called Te, the Burial Ground of Gog. And the house of Israel will bury them so that the land may be cleansed in seven months,
verses.39:13: and all the people of the land will bury them, and it will be renowned for them on the day I was glorified, says the Lord.
verses.39:14: And they will continually set apart men going throughout the land to bury those left behind upon the face of the land, to cleanse it after the seven months, and they will search thoroughly.
verses.39:15: And everyone who passes through the land and sees a human bone will build a marker beside it, until the buriers bury it in Gai, the Burial Ground of Gog.
verses.39:16: For the name of the city is also Burial Ground; and the land will be cleansed.'
verses.39:17: And you, son of man, say, 'Thus says the Lord: Speak to every winged bird and to all the wild beasts of the field, "Gather together and come, gather together from all around to My sacrifice which I have sacrificed for you, a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, and you will eat flesh and drink blood.
verses.39:18: You will eat the flesh of giants and drink the blood of the rulers of the earth—rams and calves and male goats, and the calves are all fattened.
verses.39:19: And you will eat fat to fullness, and you will drink blood to drunkenness from My sacrifice which I sacrificed for you.
verses.39:20: And you will be filled at My table with horse and rider and giant and every man of war," says the Lord.
verses.39:21: And I will set My glory among you, and all the nations will see My judgment which I executed and My hand which I brought upon them.
verses.39:22: And the house of Israel will know that I am the Lord their God from this day and onward.
verses.39:23: And all the nations will know that because of their sins the house of Israel was taken captive, because they acted faithlessly against Me, and I turned My face away from them and delivered them into the hands of their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
verses.39:24: According to their impurities and according to their lawless deeds I dealt with them, and I turned My face away from them.
verses.39:25: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Now I will turn back the captivity in Jacob, and I will have mercy on the house of Israel, and I will be zealous for My holy name.
verses.39:26: And they will bear their dishonor and the wrongdoing which they committed, when they are settled upon their land in peace, and there will be no one to cause fear,
verses.39:27: when I bring them back from the nations and gather them from the lands of the nations, and I will be sanctified in them before the nations;
verses.39:28: and they will know that I am the Lord their God, when I appear to them among the nations.
verses.39:29: And I will no longer turn My face away from them, because I have poured out My fury upon the house of Israel, says the Lord, the Lord.'"
verses.40:1: And it happened in the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, in the first month, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was captured, on that day the hand of the Lord came upon me, and He brought me
verses.40:2: in a vision of God into the land of Israel, and He set me on a very high mountain, and on it was something like the structure of a city opposite.
verses.40:3: And He brought me in there, and look, a man, and his appearance was like the appearance of gleaming bronze, and in his hand was a builders' cord and a measuring reed; and he was standing at the gate.
verses.40:4: And the man said to me, "Have you seen, son of man? See with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set in your heart all that I am showing you, because for the sake of showing you, you have come in here, and you will show all that you see to the house of Israel."
verses.40:5: And look, an enclosure wall on the outside of the house all around, and in the hand of the man was a measuring reed of six cubits by a cubit and a handbreadth; and he measured the outer wall, in width equal to the reed, and its height equal to the reed.
verses.40:6: And he went into the gate facing toward the east by seven steps, and he measured the porch of the gate, equal to the reed;
verses.40:7: and the guardroom was equal to the reed in length and equal to the reed in width, and the porch between the guardrooms was six cubits; and the second guardroom was equal to the reed in width and equal to the reed in length, and the porch was five cubits;
verses.40:8: and the third guardroom was equal to the reed in width and equal to the reed in length;
verses.40:9: and the porch of the gateway near the porch of the gate was eight cubits, and the jambs were two cubits; and the porches of the gate were on the inside;
verses.40:10: and the guardrooms of the gate were guardroom opposite guardroom, three on this side and three on that side, and one measurement for the three, one measurement for the porches on this side and on that side.
verses.40:11: And he measured the width of the door of the gateway, ten cubits, and the breadth of the gateway, thirteen cubits.
verses.40:12: And there was a narrowing cubit in front of the guardrooms on this side and on that side, and the guardroom was six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.
verses.40:13: And he measured the gate from the wall of the guardroom to the wall of the guardroom, a width of twenty-five cubits; this was gate opposite gate.
verses.40:14: And the forecourt of the porch of the gate on the outside was twenty cubits, guardrooms of the gate all around.
verses.40:15: And the forecourt of the gate on the outside to the forecourt of the porch of the gate on the inside was fifty cubits.
verses.40:16: And there were hidden windows upon the guardrooms and upon the porches inside the gate of the court all around; and likewise for the porches, windows all around on the inside, and upon the porch were palm trees on this side and on that side.
verses.40:17: And he brought me into the inner court, and look, chambers and colonnades of the court all around, thirty chambers in the colonnades.
verses.40:18: And the porticoes were at the back of the gates; according to the length of the gates was the lower colonnade.
verses.40:19: And he measured the width of the court from the forecourt of the outer gate on the inside to the forecourt of the gate facing outward, a hundred cubits, the one facing toward the east. And he led me to the north,
verses.40:20: and look, a gate facing toward the north for the outer court, and he measured it, both its length and its width,
verses.40:21: and the guardrooms, three on this side and three on that side, and the jambs and the vestibules and its palm trees. And it was according to the measurements of the gate facing toward the east: fifty cubits was its length, and twenty-five cubits was its breadth.
verses.40:22: And its windows and the vestibules and its palm trees were just like the gate facing toward the east; and by seven stairs they went up to it, and the porches were on the inside.
verses.40:23: And there was a gate for the inner court facing the gate of the north, in the same manner as the gate facing toward the east; and he measured the court from gate to gate, a hundred cubits.
verses.40:24: And he led me toward the south, and look, a gate facing toward the south, and he measured it and the guardrooms and the jambs and the vestibules according to these measurements.
verses.40:25: And its windows and the vestibules all around were just like the windows of the porch; fifty cubits was its length, and twenty-five cubits was its breadth.
verses.40:26: And it had seven stairs and vestibules on the inside, and it had palm trees, one on this side and one on that side upon the jambs.
verses.40:27: And there was a gate opposite the gate of the inner court toward the south; and he measured the court from gate to gate, a hundred cubits in breadth toward the south.
verses.40:28: And he brought me into the inner court of the gate toward the south, and he measured the gate according to these measurements,
verses.40:29: and the guardrooms and the jambs and the vestibules according to these measurements, and there were windows for it and for the vestibule all around; fifty cubits was its length, and the breadth twenty-five cubits
verses.40:31: of the porch toward the outer court, and palm trees on the jamb, and eight stairs.
verses.40:32: And he brought me into the gate facing toward the east, and he measured it according to these measurements,
verses.40:33: and the guardrooms and the jambs and the vestibules according to these measurements, and there were windows for it and for vestibules all around; fifty cubits was its length, and the breadth was twenty-five cubits.
verses.40:34: And vestibules were toward the inner court, and palm trees upon the jamb on this side and on that side, and it had eight stairs.
verses.40:35: And he brought me into the gate toward the north, and he measured according to these measurements,
verses.40:36: and the guardrooms and the jambs and the vestibules, and there were windows for it all around, and for its vestibule; fifty cubits was its length, and the breadth was twenty-five cubits;
verses.40:37: and the vestibules were toward the outer court, and palm trees on the jamb on this side and on that side, and it had eight stairs.
verses.40:38: Its chambers and its doorways and its vestibules were at the second gate; there was a drain,
verses.40:39: so that they may slaughter in it the offerings for sin and for ignorance.
verses.40:40: And at the back of the channel of the burnt offerings of the gate facing toward the north were two tables toward the east at the back of the second, and of the porch of the gate were two tables toward the east.
verses.40:41: Four on this side and four on that side at the back of the gate; upon them they will slaughter the sacrifices, opposite the eight tables of the sacrifices.
verses.40:42: And four tables of the burnt offerings were of hewn stone, a cubit and a half in width, and two and a half cubits in length, and a cubit in height; upon them they will place the instruments with which they slaughter there the burnt offerings and the sacrifices.
verses.40:43: And they will have a hewn rim of a handbreadth on the inside all around, and over the tables above, coverings to be sheltered from the rain and from the dryness.
verses.40:44: And he brought me into the inner court, and look, two halls in the inner court, one at the back of the gate facing toward the north, opening toward the south, and one at the back of the gate toward the south, yet facing toward the north.
verses.40:45: And he said to me, "This hall that faces toward the south is for the priests who keep the watch of the house;
verses.40:46: and the hall that faces toward the north is for the priests who keep the watch of the altar; those are the sons of Zadok, who draw near from Levi to the Lord to minister to Him."
verses.40:47: And he measured the court, a hundred cubits in length and a hundred cubits in breadth, on its four sides, and the altar was opposite the house.
verses.40:48: And he brought me into the porch of the house. And he measured the jamb of the porch, five cubits in width on this side and five cubits on that side, and the breadth of the doorway was fourteen cubits, and the shoulders of the door of the porch were three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.
verses.40:49: And the length of the porch was twenty cubits, and the breadth was twelve cubits; and by ten steps they went up to it, and there were pillars at the porch, one on this side and one on that side.
verses.41:1: And he brought me into the temple, in which he measured the porch, six cubits in width on one side,
verses.41:2: and six cubits the breadth of the porch on the other side, and the breadth of the gateway was ten cubits, and the shoulders of the gateway were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other side. And he measured its length, forty cubits, and the breadth, twenty cubits.
verses.41:3: And he went into the inner court, and he measured the jamb of the doorway, two cubits, and the doorway, six cubits, and the shoulders of the doorway, seven cubits on one side and seven cubits on the other side.
verses.41:4: And he measured the length of the doors, forty cubits, and a breadth of twenty cubits in front of the temple. And he said, "This is the Holy of Holies."
verses.41:5: And he measured the wall of the house, six cubits, and the breadth of the side room, four cubits all around,
verses.41:6: and the side rooms were side room upon side room, thirty, three times twice; and there was an interval in the wall of the house, in the side rooms all around, so that those taking hold might be able to see, in order that they might not touch the walls of the house at all.
verses.41:7: And the breadth of the upper one of the side rooms was according to the addition from the wall, toward the upper one all around the house, so that it might be widened above, and from the lower ones they might go up to the upper stories and from the cornices to the third stories,
verses.41:8: and the thrael of the house was a height all around; the interval of the side rooms was equal to the reed of six cubits. The intervals
verses.41:9: and the breadth of the wall of the side room on the outside were five cubits, and the remaining spaces between the side rooms of the house
verses.41:10: and between the chambers had a breadth of twenty cubits, that which surrounded the house all around.
verses.41:11: And the doors of the chambers were toward the remaining space of the one door toward the north; and the one door was toward the south, and the breadth of the light of the remaining space was five cubits in width all around.
verses.41:12: And the open-air area in front of the remaining space toward the west was seventy cubits, the width of the wall of the partition was five cubits, in breadth all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
verses.41:13: And he measured opposite the house a length of a hundred cubits, and the remaining spaces and the partitions and their walls, a length of a hundred cubits,
verses.41:14: and the breadth in front of the house and the remaining spaces opposite, a hundred cubits.
verses.41:15: And he measured the length of the partition in front of the remaining space of the parts behind that house, and the remaining spaces on one side and on the other, a hundred cubits in length. And the temple and the corners and the outer porch were paneled.
verses.41:16: And there were latticed windows, narrow openings all around for the three so as to look through; and the house and the adjacent parts were covered with wood all around, and the floor and from the floor up to the windows, and the windows opened out threefold to look through.
verses.41:17: And up to near the inner one and up to the outer one, and upon the whole wall all around, on the inside and on the outside,
verses.41:18: were carved cherubim, and palm trees between cherub and cherub. The cherub had two faces,
verses.41:19: the face of a man toward the palm tree on one side and on the other, and the face of a lion toward the palm tree on one side and on the other; the house was carved throughout all around;
verses.41:20: from the floor up to the paneling, the cherubim and the palm trees were carved throughout.
verses.41:21: And the holy place and the temple, opening out, were square; in front of the sanctuary was a vision like the appearance
verses.41:22: of a wooden altar, its height three cubits, and the length two cubits, and the breadth two cubits; and it had horns, and its base and its walls were wooden. And he said to me, "This is the table that is before the face." And the temple had two doors,
verses.41:23: and the holy place had two doors;
verses.41:24: for the two swinging doors, there were two doors for the one, and two doors for the second door.
verses.41:25: And there was carving on them, and on the doors of the temple were cherubim and palm trees according to the carving of the sanctuary, and sturdy timbers in front of the porch on the outside,
verses.41:26: and hidden windows. And he measured on one side and on the other, to the roofings of the porch, and the side rooms of the house were yoked together.
verses.42:1: And he brought me into the inner court toward the east, opposite the gate toward the north; and he brought me in, and look, five chambers adjoining the remaining space and adjoining the partition toward the north,
verses.42:2: for a hundred cubits in length toward the north, and the width fifty,
verses.42:3: laid out in the same way as the gates of the inner court and in the same way as the colonnades of the outer court, arranged in rows facing one another, threefold porticoes.
verses.42:4: And opposite the chambers was a walkway ten cubits in width, for a hundred cubits in length; and their doorways were toward the north,
verses.42:5: and the upper walkways were likewise; for the colonnade projected from it, from the lower colonnade, and the interval; thus there was a colonnade and an interval, and thus two porticoes.
verses.42:6: For they were triple, and they did not have pillars like the pillars of the outer ones; for this reason they projected from the lower ones and the middle ones from the ground.
verses.42:7: And there was a light on the outside, in the same way as the chambers of the outer court that face opposite the chambers toward the north, a length of fifty cubits.
verses.42:8: For the length of the chambers facing toward the outer court was fifty cubits, and these are the ones facing opposite those; the total was a hundred cubits.
verses.42:9: And the doors of these chambers were of the entrance toward the east, for going in through them from the outer court
verses.42:10: according to the light of the walkway at the beginning; and the parts toward the south were in front of the south, in front of the remaining space and in front of the partition; and the chambers
verses.42:11: and the walkway in front of them were according to the measurements of the chambers toward the north, and according to their length, and according to their breadth, and according to all their exits, and according to all their turnings, and according to their lights, and according to their doorways,
verses.42:12: of the chambers toward the south, and according to the doorways from the beginning of the walkway toward a light of a reed's interval, and toward the east for going in through them.
verses.42:13: And he said to me, "The chambers toward the north and the chambers toward the south, which are in front of the intervals, these are the chambers of the holy place, in which the priests, the sons of Zadok, who draw near to the Lord, will eat the most holy things there; and there they will place the most holy things, and the sacrifice, and the offerings for sin, and the offerings for ignorance, because the place is holy.
verses.42:14: No one shall enter there except the priests; they shall not go out from the holy place into the outer court, so that those who approach may be continually holy; and let them not touch their vestments in which they minister, because they are holy; and they shall put on other garments whenever they touch the people."
verses.42:15: And the measurement of the house on the inside was completed. And he brought me out by the way of the gate that faces toward the east, and he measured the pattern of the house all around in order.
verses.42:16: And he stood at the back of the gate that faces toward the east, and he measured five hundred with the measuring reed.
verses.42:17: And he turned toward the north and measured the side facing the north, five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.
verses.42:18: And he turned toward the west and measured the side facing the west, five hundred with the measuring reed.
verses.42:19: And he turned toward the south and measured opposite the south, five hundred with the measuring reed,
verses.42:20: the four sides of the same reed; and he arranged it and their enclosure all around, five hundred toward the east and five hundred cubits in breadth, to separate between the sanctuary and the outer wall that was in the arrangement of the house.
verses.43:1: And he led me to the gate that faces toward the east, and he brought me out.
verses.43:2: And look, the glory of the God of Israel was coming by the way toward the east, and the sound of the encampment was like the sound of many redoubling; and the earth shone forth like radiance from the glory all around.
verses.43:3: And the vision that I saw was like the vision that I saw when I went in to anoint the city, and the vision of the chariot that I saw was like the vision that I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face.
verses.43:4: And the glory of the Lord entered into the house by the way of the gate that faces toward the east.
verses.43:5: And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and look, the house was full of the glory of the Lord.
verses.43:6: And I stood, and look, there was a voice from the house of One speaking to me, and the man was standing beside me.
verses.43:7: And He said to me, "You have seen, son of man, the place of My throne and the place of the sole of My feet, in which My name will dwell in the midst of the house of Israel forever. And the house of Israel will no longer profane My holy name, they and their rulers, in their prostitution and in the murders of the rulers in their midst,
verses.43:8: by their setting My threshold with their thresholds and My doorposts next to their doorposts; and they made My wall as adjoining between Me and them, and they profaned My holy name in their lawless deeds that they practiced; and I destroyed them in My wrath and in slaughter.
verses.43:9: And now let them put away their prostitution and the murders of their rulers from Me, and I will dwell in their midst forever.
verses.43:10: And you, son of man, show the house to the house of Israel, and they will cease from their sins; and its appearance and its arrangement,
verses.43:11: and they themselves will bear their punishment for all that they have done. And you shall outline the house and its exits and its foundation, and all its ordinances and all its statutes you shall make known to them and outline before them, and they shall keep all My decrees and all My ordinances and do them.
verses.43:12: And the outline of the house on the top of the mountain: all its boundaries all around are most holy."
verses.43:13: And these are the measurements of the altar by the cubit of a cubit and a handbreadth: a hollow of a cubit in depth, and a cubit the width, and a rim on its edge all around of a span. And this is the height of the altar:
verses.43:14: from the depth of the beginning of its hollow to this great propitiatory below is two cubits, and the width is a cubit. And from the small propitiatory to the great propitiatory is four cubits, and the width is a cubit.
verses.43:15: And the ariel is four cubits, and from the ariel and above the horns is a cubit.
verses.43:16: And the ariel is twelve cubits in length by twelve cubits, square on its four sides.
verses.43:17: And the propitiatory is fourteen cubits in length by fourteen cubits in width on its four sides, and the rim for it all around, encircling it, is half a cubit, and its circuit is a cubit all around; and its steps face toward the east.
verses.43:18: And He said to me, "Son of man, thus says the Lord God of Israel: These are the ordinances of the altar on the day of its making, to offer up burnt offerings on it and to pour blood against it.
verses.43:19: And you shall give to the priests, the Levites, who are from the seed of Zadok, who draw near to Me, says the Lord God, to minister to Me, a young bull from the herd for a sin offering.
verses.43:20: And they shall take from its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar and on the four corners of the propitiatory and on the base all around, and they shall make atonement for it.
verses.43:21: And they shall take the young bull for the sin offering, and it shall be burned up in the set-apart place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
verses.43:22: And on the second day they shall take two unblemished kids of the goats for a sin offering, and they shall make atonement for the altar just as they made atonement with the young bull.
verses.43:23: And after you finish the atonement, they shall present an unblemished young bull from the herd and an unblemished ram from the sheep,
verses.43:24: and you shall present them before the Lord; and the priests shall cast salt on them and offer them up as burnt offerings to the Lord.
verses.43:25: For seven days you shall prepare a kid for a sin offering each day, and a young bull from the herd and a ram from the sheep; unblemished ones they shall prepare
verses.43:26: for seven days. And they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and they shall fill their hands.
verses.43:27: And it shall be from the eighth day and onward, the priests shall prepare on the altar your burnt offerings and your offerings of deliverance; and I will accept you, says the Lord."
verses.44:1: And he brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary that faces toward the east, and it was shut.
verses.44:2: And the Lord said to me, "This gate shall be shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall pass through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, will enter through it, and it shall be shut.
verses.44:3: For the ruler, he shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord; he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and by its way he shall go out."
verses.44:4: And he brought me in by the way of the gate toward the north, in front of the house; and I looked, and look, the house of the Lord was full of glory, and I fell on my face.
verses.44:5: And the Lord said to me, "Son of man, set it in your heart, and see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I speak with you concerning all the ordinances of the house of the Lord and concerning all its statutes; and you shall set your heart on the entrance of the house, according to all its exits in all the holy places.
verses.44:6: And you shall say to the provoking house, to the house of Israel, 'Thus says the Lord God: Let it be enough for you from all your lawless deeds, house of Israel,
verses.44:7: in your bringing in foreign sons, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My sanctuary; and they were profaning it when you presented loaves, flesh, and blood, and you were transgressing My covenant in all your lawless deeds,
verses.44:8: and you gave orders to keep charges in My sanctuary.
verses.44:9: Therefore thus says the Lord God: No foreign son, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into My sanctuary, among all the sons of foreigners who are in the midst of the house of Israel,
verses.44:10: but rather the Levites who sprang away from Me when Israel went astray from Me after their own devices—and they shall bear their unrighteousness,
verses.44:11: and they shall be in My sanctuary ministering, gatekeepers at the gates of the house and ministering to the house; they shall slaughter the burnt offerings and the sacrifices for the people, and they shall stand before the people to minister to them.
verses.44:12: Because they ministered to them before the face of their idols, and it became to the house of Israel a punishment of unrighteousness, on account of this I lifted up My hand against them, says the Lord God,
verses.44:13: and they shall not draw near to Me to serve as priests to Me, nor to approach the holy things of the sons of Israel nor My most holy things; and they shall bear their dishonor in the straying by which they went astray.
verses.44:14: And they shall bring them down to keep charges of the house, for all its works and for all that they may do.
verses.44:15: The priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charges of My sanctuary when the house of Israel went astray from Me, these shall approach Me to minister to Me, and they shall stand before My face to present to Me sacrifice, fat and blood, says the Lord God.
verses.44:16: These shall enter into My sanctuary, and these shall come near to My table to minister to Me, and they shall keep My charges.
verses.44:17: And it shall be, when they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall put on linen robes; and they shall not put on wool while they minister from the gate of the inner court.
verses.44:18: And they shall have linen turbans on their heads, and they shall have linen breeches on their loins, and they shall not gird themselves by force.
verses.44:19: And when they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall take off their robes in which they minister, and they shall place them in the chambers of the sanctuary, and they shall put on other robes, and they shall by no means sanctify the people with their robes.
verses.44:20: And they shall not shave their heads, and they shall not strip bare their hair; they shall surely cover their heads.
verses.44:21: And no priest shall drink wine when they enter into the inner court.
verses.44:22: And they shall not take for themselves as a wife a widow or a divorced woman, but only a virgin from the seed of Israel; yet a widow, if she is from a priest, they may take.
verses.44:23: And they shall teach My people the difference between the holy and the profane, and they shall make known to them the difference between the clean and the unclean.
verses.44:24: And over a judgment of blood these shall stand to decide; they shall uphold My decrees, and they shall judge My judgments, and they shall keep My statutes and My ordinances in all My feasts, and they shall sanctify My Sabbaths.
verses.44:25: And they shall not go in to the soul of a person to be defiled; except for a father and a mother, and for a son and for a daughter, and for a brother and for his sister who has not belonged to a husband, he may be defiled.
verses.44:26: And after he is cleansed, he shall count out seven days for himself;
verses.44:27: and on whatever day they enter into the inner court to minister in the holy place, they shall present a propitiation, says the Lord God.
verses.44:28: And it shall be to them for an inheritance: I am an inheritance to them; and no possession shall be given to them among the sons of Israel, because I am their possession.
verses.44:29: And the sacrifices and the offerings for sin and the offerings for ignorance they themselves shall eat, and every set-apart thing in Israel shall be theirs.
verses.44:30: The firstfruits of all things and the firstborn of all things and all the contributions from all your firstfruits shall belong to the priests. And your first produce you shall give to the priest, to place your blessings upon your houses.
verses.44:31: And anything that dies of itself or is caught by wild beasts, from the birds or from the livestock, the priests shall not eat.'"
verses.45:1: And when you measure out the land for an inheritance, you shall set apart a firstfruit offering to the Lord, a holy portion from the land, twenty-five thousand in length and twenty thousand in width; it shall be holy within all its borders all around.
verses.45:2: And from this there shall be a sanctuary, five hundred by five hundred, square all around, and fifty cubits of open space for it all around.
verses.45:3: And from this measurement you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of twenty thousand, and in it shall be the Holy of Holies.
verses.45:4: From the land it shall belong to the priests who minister in the holy place, and it shall belong to those who draw near to minister to the Lord; and it shall be a place for them for houses set apart for their sanctification,
verses.45:5: twenty-five thousand in length and twenty thousand in width. And for the Levites who minister in the house, they shall have cities to live in as a possession.
verses.45:6: And you shall give the possession of the city, five thousand in width and twenty-five thousand in length, just like the firstfruit offering of the sanctuary; they shall belong to the whole house of Israel.
verses.45:7: And for the ruler, on one side and on the other toward the firstfruit offerings of the sanctuary, toward the possession of the city, facing the firstfruit offerings of the sanctuary and facing the possession of the city, the parts toward the sea and from the parts toward the sea toward the east; and the length shall be like one of the portions, from the borders toward the sea, and the length to the borders toward the east of the land.
verses.45:8: And it shall be for him as a possession in Israel, and the rulers of Israel shall no longer oppress My people; and the house of Israel shall inherit the land according to their tribes.
verses.45:9: Thus says the Lord God: "Let it be enough for you, rulers of Israel! Put away injustice and misery; do justice and righteousness; remove oppression from My people," says the Lord God.
verses.45:10: "You shall have a just balance and a just measure and a just choenix of the measure,
verses.45:11: and the choenix shall likewise be one for holding: a tenth of the homer is a choenix, and a tenth of the homer; according to the homer shall be the equivalent.
verses.45:12: And the weights shall be twenty obols; five shekels are five, and ten shekels, and fifty shekels shall be the mina for you.
verses.45:13: And this is the firstfruit offering that you shall set apart: a sixth of a measure from the homer of wheat, and the sixth of the ephah itself from the kor of barley.
verses.45:14: And the statute for the oil: a cotyle of oil from ten cotyles, for the ten cotyles are a homer.
verses.45:15: And a sheep from the sheep, out of ten, a portion set apart from all the families of Israel, for sacrifices and for burnt offerings and for deliverance offerings, to make atonement for you," says the Lord God.
verses.45:16: And all the people shall give this firstfruit offering to the ruler of Israel.
verses.45:17: And through the ruler shall be the burnt offerings and the sacrifices and the drink offerings at the feasts and at the new moons and on the Sabbaths and at all the feasts of the house of Israel; he himself shall prepare the offerings for sin and the sacrifice and the burnt offerings and the deliverance offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
verses.45:18: Thus says the Lord God: "In the first month, on the first of the month, you shall take an unblemished calf from the cattle to make atonement for the holy place.
verses.45:19: And the priest shall take some of the blood of the atonement, and he shall put it on the doorposts of the house and on the four corners of the temple and on the altar and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
verses.45:20: And thus you shall do in the seventh month, on the first of the month, a portion from each one, and you shall make atonement for the house.
verses.45:21: And in the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, the Passover shall be a feast for you; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.45:22: And on that day the ruler shall prepare, for himself and the house and for all the people of the land, a calf for sin.
verses.45:23: And during the seven days of the feast he shall prepare burnt offerings to the Lord: seven calves and seven rams, unblemished, daily for the seven days, and for sin a kid of the goats daily, and a sacrifice.
verses.45:24: And you shall prepare a cake for the calf and a cake for the ram, and a hin of oil for the cake.
verses.45:25: And in the seventh month, on the fifteenth of the month, at the feast, you shall do the same for seven days: just like the offerings for sin, and just like the burnt offerings, and just like the grain offering, and just like the oil."
verses.46:1: Thus says the Lord God: "The gate in the inner court that faces east shall be shut during the six working days; on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.
verses.46:2: And the ruler shall enter by the way of the porch of the inner gate and stand at the doorway of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his burnt offerings and his deliverance offerings.
verses.46:3: And he shall worship at the doorway of the gate and go out, and the gate shall not be shut until evening; and the people of the land shall worship at the doorway of that gate both on the Sabbaths and at the new moons before the Lord.
verses.46:4: And the ruler shall offer the burnt offerings to the Lord on the Sabbath day: six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram,
verses.46:5: and a grain offering, a cake for the ram, and for the lambs a sacrifice, a gift of his hand, and a hin of oil for the cake.
verses.46:6: And on the day of the new moon, an unblemished calf and six lambs, and there shall be an unblemished ram,
verses.46:7: and a cake for the ram and a cake for the calf shall be a grain offering, and for the lambs as much as his hand is able, and a hin of oil for the cake.
verses.46:8: And when the ruler enters, he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and by the way of the gate he shall go out.
verses.46:9: And whenever the people of the land enter before the Lord at the feasts, the one who enters by the way of the gate facing north to worship shall go out by the way of the gate toward the south, and the one who enters by the way of the gate toward the south shall go out by the way of the gate toward the north; he shall not return by the gate into which he has entered, but shall go out straight opposite it.
verses.46:10: And the ruler in their midst, when they enter, shall enter with them, and when they go out, he shall go out.
verses.46:11: And at the feasts and at the festive assemblies, the grain offering shall be a cake for the calf and a cake for the ram, and for the lambs as much as his hand is able, and a hin of oil for the cake.
verses.46:12: And if the ruler prepares a freewill offering, a burnt offering of deliverance to the Lord, then he shall open for himself the gate facing east, and he shall prepare his burnt offering and his deliverance offerings in the same manner as he does on the Sabbath day; and he shall go out, and he shall shut the doors after he goes out.
verses.46:13: And he shall prepare a year-old unblemished lamb for a burnt offering daily to the Lord; in the morning he shall prepare it.
verses.46:14: And he shall prepare a grain offering with it in the morning, a sixth of the measure, and a third of a hin of oil to mix the fine flour, a grain offering to the Lord, a perpetual statute.
verses.46:15: You shall prepare the lamb, and you shall prepare the grain offering and the oil in the morning, a continual burnt offering."
verses.46:16: Thus says the Lord God: "If the ruler gives a gift to one of his sons from his inheritance, this shall belong to his sons as a possession by inheritance.
verses.46:17: But if he gives a gift to one of his servants, it shall belong to him until the year of release, and he shall return it to the ruler; only as for the inheritance of his sons, it shall belong to them.
verses.46:18: And the ruler shall certainly not take from the inheritance of the people to oppress them; from his own possession he shall give an inheritance to his sons, so that My people may not be scattered, each one from his possession."
verses.46:19: And he brought me into the entrance behind the gate, into the chamber of the holy things of the priests facing north, and look, there was a place set apart there.
verses.46:20: And he said to me, "This is the place where the priests shall boil the offerings for ignorance and the offerings for sin, and there they shall bake the grain offering, so as not to carry them out at all into the outer court to sanctify the people."
verses.46:21: And he brought me out into the outer court, and he led me around to the four parts of the court, and look, there was a court at the sides of the court;
verses.46:22: at each side a court, a court at the four parts, and of the court there was a small court, forty cubits in length and thirty cubits in width, one measure for the four.
verses.46:23: And there were chambers all around in them, all around the four; and kitchens were made underneath the chambers all around.
verses.46:24: And he said to me, "These are the houses of the cooks, where those who minister in the house shall boil the sacrifices of the people."
verses.47:1: And he brought me to the doorway of the house, and look, water was flowing out from beneath the atrium toward the east, for the front of the house faced east; and the water was flowing down from the right side, from the south, toward the altar.
verses.47:2: And he brought me out by the way of the gate toward the north, and he led me around by the outside way to the gate of the court facing east, and look, the water was streaming down from the right side,
verses.47:3: like the going out of a man from the opposite side. And there was a measure in his hand; and he measured a thousand with the measure, and he passed through in the water, water of release;
verses.47:4: and he measured a thousand, and he passed through in the water, water up to the thighs; and he measured a thousand, and he passed through water up to the waist.
verses.47:5: And he measured a thousand, and he was not able to pass through, for it was surging wildly, a torrent that they will not cross.
verses.47:6: And he said to me, "Have you seen, son of man?" And he led me to the bank of the river
verses.47:7: upon my return; and look, on the bank of the river there were very many trees on this side and on that.
verses.47:8: And he said to me, "This water that flows out into Galilee toward the east, and went down to Arabia, and came all the way to the sea, to the water of the outlet, and it will heal the waters,
verses.47:9: and it shall be that every soul of the creatures that swarm, in all places where the river comes there, shall live; and there shall be very many fish there, because this water has come there, and it will heal and live; everything to which the river comes there shall live.
verses.47:10: And fishermen shall stand there from En-gedi to En-eglaim; it shall be a drying place for dragnets, it shall be by itself; and its fish shall be like the fish of the Great Sea, a very great multitude.
verses.47:11: And in its outlet and in its turning back and in its overflowing, they shall certainly not heal; they have been given over to salt.
verses.47:12: And by the river there shall grow up, on its bank on this side and on that, every tree for food; it shall certainly not grow old upon it, nor shall its fruit fail; in its newness it shall bear firstfruits, because their waters, these flow out from the sanctuary; and their fruit shall be for food, and their growth shall be for healing."
verses.47:13: Thus says the Lord God: "These are the borders of the land that you shall inherit: for the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel, an addition of a measured portion.
verses.47:14: And you shall inherit it, each one just like his brother, concerning which I lifted up My hand to give it to their fathers; and this land shall fall to you as an inheritance.
verses.47:15: And these are the borders of the land toward the north: from the Great Sea that goes down and splits around, the entrance of Hamath, Seldamma,
verses.47:16: Abthera, Sibraim, Heliam, between the borders of Damascus and the borders of Hamath, the court of Saunan, which are above the borders of Auranitis.
verses.47:17: These are the borders from the sea: from the court of Enan, the borders of Damascus, and the parts toward the north.
verses.47:18: And the parts toward the east: between Loranitis and Damascus, and between Gilead and the land of Israel, the Jordan marks the boundary to the sea east of Palm Grove; these are the parts toward the east.
verses.47:19: And the parts toward the south and southwest: from Teman and Palm Grove, to the water of Marimoth-kadem, extending along to the Great Sea;
verses.47:20: this part is south and southwest. This part of the Great Sea marks the boundary, as far as opposite the entrance of Hamath, as far as its entrance; these are the parts toward the sea of Hamath.
verses.47:21: And you shall divide this land among them, the tribes of Israel.
verses.47:22: You shall cast it by lot for yourselves and for the proselytes who reside in your midst, who have fathered sons in your midst, and they shall be yours like native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they shall eat in an inheritance in the midst of the tribes of Israel,
verses.47:23: and they shall be in a tribe of proselytes, among the proselytes who are with them; there you shall give them an inheritance," says the Lord God.
verses.48:1: And these are the names of the tribes, from the beginning on the north, along the side of the descent of that which cuts around to the entrance of Hamath, the court of Ailam, the border of Damascus toward the north along the side of Hamath, the court; and the east side as far as the sea shall belong to them: Dan, one.
verses.48:2: And from the borders of Dan, the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Asher, one.
verses.48:3: And from the borders of Asher, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Naphtali, one.
verses.48:4: And from the borders of Naphtali, from the east as far as the side toward the sea: Manasseh, one.
verses.48:5: And from the borders of Manasseh, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Ephraim, one.
verses.48:6: And from the borders of Ephraim, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Reuben, one.
verses.48:7: And from the borders of Reuben, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Judah, one.
verses.48:8: And from the borders of Judah, from the east side it shall remain; the firstfruit of the setting apart shall be twenty-five thousand in width, and in length like one of the portions from the east side and as far as the side toward the sea, and the holy place shall be in the midst of them.
verses.48:9: The firstfruit which they shall set apart to the Lord shall be twenty-five thousand in length and twenty-five thousand in width.
verses.48:10: Of these shall be the firstfruit of the holy places for the priests: toward the north twenty-five thousand, and toward the sea ten thousand, and toward the south twenty-five thousand; and the mountain of the holy places shall be in the midst of it;
verses.48:11: for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the charges of the house, who did not go astray in the straying of the sons of Israel, in the way that the Levites went astray.
verses.48:12: And the firstfruit shall be given to them from the firstfruits of the land, a holy of holies, from the borders of the Levites.
verses.48:13: And for the Levites, what is adjacent to the borders of the priests shall be twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width; the entire length shall be twenty-five thousand, and the width twenty thousand.
verses.48:14: None of it shall be sold, nor measured out, nor shall the first produce of the land be taken away, for it is holy to the Lord.
verses.48:15: And as for the five thousand that remain in breadth alongside the twenty-five thousand, it shall be an outer wall for the city, for dwelling and for its open space; and the city shall be in the midst of it.
verses.48:16: And these are its measurements: on the north side, four thousand five hundred; and on the south side, four thousand five hundred; and on the east side, four thousand five hundred; and on the side toward the sea, four thousand five hundred.
verses.48:17: And there shall be an open space for the city: toward the north two hundred fifty, and toward the south two hundred fifty, and toward the east two hundred fifty, and toward the sea two hundred fifty.
verses.48:18: And the remainder of the length, adjacent to the firstfruits of the holy places, shall be ten thousand toward the east and ten thousand toward the sea; and they shall be the firstfruits of the holy place, and its produce shall be for bread for those who work the city.
verses.48:19: And those who work the city shall work it from all the tribes of Israel.
verses.48:20: The entire firstfruit shall be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand; as a square you shall set apart there the beginning of the holy place, from the possession of the city.
verses.48:21: And the remainder shall belong to the ruler, on this side and on that side, from the firstfruits of the holy place and to the possession of the city, along twenty-five thousand in length as far as the borders toward the east, and toward the sea along twenty-five thousand as far as the borders toward the sea, adjacent to the portions of the ruler; and the firstfruit of the holy places and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the midst of it.
verses.48:22: And from the Levites, from the possession of the city, it shall be in the midst of the rulers, between the borders of Judah and the borders of Benjamin; it shall belong to the rulers.
verses.48:23: And as for the remainder of the tribes, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Benjamin, one.
verses.48:24: And from the borders of Benjamin, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Simeon, one.
verses.48:25: And from the borders of Simeon, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Issachar, one.
verses.48:26: And from the borders of Issachar, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Zebulun, one.
verses.48:27: And from the borders of Zebulun, from the east side as far as the side toward the sea: Gad, one.
verses.48:28: And from the borders of Gad as far as the side toward the southwest, then its borders shall be from Teman and the water of Barimoth Kadesh, of an inheritance, as far as the Great Sea.
verses.48:29: This is the land which you shall cast by lot for the tribes of Israel, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.
verses.48:30: And these are the exits of the city: those toward the north, four thousand five hundred by measure.
verses.48:31: And the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel; three gates toward the north: the gate of Reuben, one; and the gate of Judah, one; and the gate of Levi, one.
verses.48:32: And the east side, four thousand five hundred; and three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; and the gate of Benjamin, one; and the gate of Dan, one.
verses.48:33: And the south side, four thousand five hundred by measure; and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; and the gate of Issachar, one; and the gate of Zebulun, one.
verses.48:34: And the side toward the sea, four thousand five hundred by measure; and three gates: the gate of Gad, one; and the gate of Asher, one; and the gate of Naphtali, one.
verses.48:35: The circumference shall be eighteen thousand. And the name of the city, from whatever day it comes into being, shall be its name.

notes.1:2: Greek reads "Ioakeim" (corresponding to Jehoiakim), a form the Septuagint frequently uses for both Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin (the latter being named in the Hebrew text here).
notes.1:7: The Greek text uniquely describes the creatures' feet as "winged" and adds that "their wings were light," differing substantially from the Hebrew description of calf-like feet.
notes.1:13: Verse 14 of the Hebrew text (describing the living creatures darting to and fro like lightning) is absent in the Septuagint.
notes.1:16: Greek "tharseis" transliterates the Hebrew gemstone term "tarshish" (often identified as beryl or chrysolite).
notes.1:18: Greek literally renders the wheel rims as "backs" ("notoi"), connects them to the preceding verse ("nor did their backs"), and reads "and I saw them" where the Hebrew text reads "and they were awesome."
notes.2:1: In the Septuagint versification, the opening sentence ("This was the vision... One speaking") begins chapter 2 rather than concluding 1:28 as in the Hebrew text.
notes.2:2: Greek πνεῦμα here is anarthrous (without the definite article) and can be rendered either "the Spirit" (capitalized) or "a spirit" / "wind"; similarly, αὐτοῦ ("Him") can refer either to the Lord speaking or to the spirit/voice.
notes.2:3: Greek "parapikraino" ("provoke," literally "embitter") renders the Hebrew root for rebellion throughout chapters 2-3.
notes.2:5: Greek reads "are terrified" (also in 2:7), whereas the Hebrew text reads "refuse" or "forbear."
notes.2:6: Greek translates the Hebrew nouns for "briers and thorns" as verbs, reading "they will rage and band together against you all around."
notes.3:2: Greek reads the third-person verb "He opened my mouth," whereas the Hebrew text reads the first-person "I opened my mouth."
notes.3:8: Greek uses "contentious" (3:7) and "contention" (3:8), followed by "continually stronger than rock" (3:9), differing from the Hebrew references to a hard forehead and emery/flint.
notes.3:12: Greek πνεῦμα here is anarthrous and can be rendered either "the Spirit" or "a spirit" / "a wind."
notes.3:13: Greek literally reads "I saw the sound of the wings," supplying the verb "I saw" before the sound of the flapping wings.
notes.3:14: Greek τὸ πνεῦμα ("the spirit" / "the wind") refers back to the anarthrous πνεῦμα of 3:12 and can be rendered either capitalized ("the Spirit") or lowercase ("the spirit" / "the wind").
notes.3:15: Instead of the Hebrew place-name "Tel-abib" and "stunned," Greek reads "aloft" ("meteoros"), adds "I went around," and concludes with "moving about in their midst."
notes.3:20: Greek renders the Hebrew term for "stumbling block" as "the torment" ("ten basanon"), a characteristic Septuagint Ezekiel rendering; in 3:17, Greek likewise uses the stronger verb "threaten" ("diapeileomai") alongside "warn" ("diastellomai") in 3:18-21.
notes.3:24: Greek πνεῦμα here is anarthrous and can be rendered either "the Spirit" or "a spirit" / "wind"; the subject of "spoke" (ἐλάλησεν) is unexpressed in Greek and may refer either to the Lord ("He") or to the spirit.
notes.4:4: The Septuagint specifies 150 days for Israel here and 190 days in 4:5 and 4:9 (combining Israel's 150 days and Judah's 40 days in 4:6), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has no number in 4:4 and 390 days in 4:5 and 4:9.
notes.4:5: Greek "their two iniquities" (tas duo adikias auton) reflects reading the unvocalized Hebrew consonants for "years of" as "two," referring to the combined periods of Israel and Judah totaling 190 days.
notes.4:7: Greek "you shall strengthen your arm" (stereoseis) differs from the Masoretic Text's "with your arm bared."
notes.4:14: Greek ei here serves as an asseverative particle ("surely"), likely an itacistic spelling of e ("truly, surely"); "from my birth" and "stale meat" follow the Septuagint wording rather than the Hebrew's "from my youth" and "tainted meat."
notes.5:2: The Septuagint divides the hair into four fourths (to tetarton four times, matching 5:12), including a doubled burning clause, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text divides it into three thirds.
notes.5:6: Greek "you shall speak My ordinances to the lawless one" reflects reading the Hebrew verb "she rebelled" as "you shall speak" and rendering "wickedness" as a personal dative.
notes.5:12: Greek thanatos ("death") is the Septuagint's regular rendering of Hebrew "pestilence" in the judgment triad of sword, famine, and death (see also 5:17; 6:11-12).
notes.5:14: Greek "and your daughters around you" (referring to Jerusalem's surrounding satellite towns) differs from the Masoretic Text's "and a reproach among the nations around you."
notes.5:15: The rare Greek adjective pair stenakte kai delaiste ("lamented and wretched") includes the Septuagint hapax legomenon delaiste, glossed in ancient lexica as "wretched" or "miserable."
notes.6:4: Greek temene ("shrines" or "sacred precincts") renders Hebrew "incense altars," and traumatias (literally "wounded") is the standard Septuagint equivalent for Hebrew "slain" (also in 6:7, 13).
notes.6:9: Greek omomoka ("I have sworn") reflects reading the Hebrew consonants for "I was broken" as "I have sworn," and "their practices" and "beat their faces" follow the distinctive Septuagint text.
notes.6:11: Greek euge euge ("Aha, aha!", literally "Well done, well done!") expresses mocking exultation, contrasting with the Hebrew interjection "Alas!"
notes.6:14: Deblatha is the Septuagint proper name (Deblatha) corresponding to Hebrew Diblathah ("toward Diblah," often emended to Riblah); the Greek reads "from the wilderness of Deblatha" rather than the Masoretic Text's "more desolate than the wilderness toward Diblah."
notes.7:4: The Septuagint arranges 7:3-9 in a different sequence from the Hebrew Masoretic Text and reads "not with tumults nor with birth pains" rather than the Hebrew "tumult, and not joyful shouting of mountains."
notes.7:7: The Greek reads literally "I will send against you" without an expressed object, reflecting a variant reading ("I") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "My anger."
notes.7:13: The Greek phrase "in the eye of his life" reflects a textual difference from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "in his iniquity."
notes.7:23: The Greek reads "confusion" rather than the Hebrew "chain," and "peoples" rather than the Hebrew "bloody crimes" (compare 9:9).
notes.7:25: The Greek reads "propitiation" (exilasmos) as the subject that comes and seeks peace, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "anguish."
notes.8:1: The Septuagint dates this vision to the "fifth month," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads the "sixth month."
notes.8:3: The Greek "pillar of the acquirer" reflects a different reading or vocalization of the Hebrew behind the Masoretic Text's "image of jealousy." Also, Greek πνεῦμα ("the Spirit") is anarthrous and can alternatively be rendered "a spirit" or "a wind."
notes.8:5: The Greek omits the Hebrew's mention of the "image of jealousy" here and reads "facing east" where the Hebrew reads "of the altar."
notes.8:11: The Greek gives the name "Jeconiah" (Iechonias), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Jaazaniah."
notes.8:16: The Greek reads "about twenty men" rather than the Hebrew's "about twenty-five men," and renders "porticoes" with the plural transliteration ton ailam.
notes.9:2: The Greek reads "a full-length robe" and "a sash of sapphire," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "linen" and "a scribe's writing case."
notes.9:3: The Greek reads "open court" (aithrion) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "threshold."
notes.9:9: The Greek reads "many peoples" and "injustice and uncleanness" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "blood" and "perversity."
notes.10:5: Greek "theou Saddai" transliterates the Hebrew divine epithet El Shaddai ("God Shaddai") rather than translating it as "Almighty."
notes.10:7: The Greek text leaves the subject of "stretched out his hand" unexpressed (whereas the Hebrew specifies "the cherub"), and speaks of "the holy robe" here and in v. 6 rather than "linen."
notes.10:13: Greek "Gelgel" transliterates Hebrew galgal ("whirling wheels" or "wheelwork"); verse 14 of the Hebrew text, which describes the four faces, is absent from the Greek text.
notes.10:21: The Greek text reads "eight wings" (okto pteryges), whereas the Hebrew text reads "four wings."
notes.11:1: The Greek text names "Jeconiah the son of Ezer" (Iechonian ton tou Ezer), whereas the Hebrew text reads "Jaazaniah the son of Azzur." Also, Greek πνεῦμα ("the Spirit") is anarthrous and can alternatively be rendered "a spirit" or "a wind."
notes.11:3: The Greek reads "Have the houses not recently been built?" rather than the Hebrew "the time is not near to build houses."
notes.11:5: Greek πνεῦμα here is anarthrous and lacks "of the Lord" (contrast MT); it can be rendered either "the Spirit" or "a spirit."
notes.11:10: The Greek reads "on the mountains of Israel" (epi ton oreon tou Israel, vs. Hebrew "at the border of Israel"), and verses 11-12 of the Hebrew text are absent from the Greek text.
notes.11:15: The Greek reads "the men of your captivity" (vs. Hebrew "your kindred") and "have been brought to an end" (syntetelestai), reflecting a reading of Hebrew kallah ("be finished") rather than kulloh ("all of it").
notes.11:19: The Greek text reads "a different heart" (kardian heteran), whereas the Hebrew text reads "one heart."
notes.11:24: The Greek text reads "And I went up from the vision that I saw" (first person), whereas the Hebrew reads "Then the vision that I had seen went up from me." Both occurrences of πνεῦμα here ("the Spirit" and "the Spirit of God") are anarthrous in Greek and can alternatively be rendered "a spirit" / "a wind" and "a spirit of God."
notes.12:2: The Greek text reads "in the midst of their injustices" (en meso ton adikion auton), whereas the Hebrew reads "in the midst of the rebellious house."
notes.12:6: The Greek reads the passive "you will be lifted up on shoulders" and "concealed" (also in vv. 7 and 12), whereas the Hebrew speaks of carrying baggage on the shoulder "in the dark."
notes.12:10: The Greek uses the double divine title "kyrios Kyrios" ("the Lord, the Lord") and reads "The prince and the leader" (Ho archon kai ho aphegoumenos), where the Hebrew has "This oracle concerns the prince."
notes.13:5: The Greek text differs notably from the Hebrew ("in the breaches" / "built up a wall"), reading "in steadfastness" (en stereomati) and "they gathered flocks" (synegagon poimnia), and omitting "in battle" before "In the day of the Lord."
notes.13:9: Greek paideia ("instruction" or "discipline") stands where the Hebrew has "council," and the final verb is third person plural ("they will know") rather than second person.
notes.13:10: Here and in vv. 11, 14, and 15, the Greek renders the Hebrew word for "whitewash" as the future verb "it will fall" (peseitai).
notes.13:14: Greek met' elenchon ("with rebukes") reflects a different reading of the Hebrew consonants underlying "in its midst."
notes.13:20: Greek kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord," also in 14:6) reflects the doubled Hebrew divine title Adonai YHWH. Greek systrephete ("round up"), ekstrephete ("twist away"), and "into dispersion" (eis diaskorpismon) also diverge from the Hebrew bird-hunting imagery.
notes.14:3: Throughout vv. 3-7, the Greek renders Hebrew "idols" with "thoughts" (dianoemata, vv. 3-4) and "devices" (enthymemata, vv. 5, 7), and translates "stumbling block" as "punishment" (kolasin).
notes.14:5: Greek plagiase ("may turn aside" or "outflank") is third person singular (continuing "his mind" from v. 4, or an indefinite subject) where the Hebrew has "so that I may seize."
notes.14:9: Greek planese is active ("misleads," or intransitively "goes astray") where the Hebrew has a passive verb ("is deceived").
notes.14:19: Here and in v. 21, the Greek translates Hebrew "pestilence" as "death" (thanaton).
notes.14:23: The Greek text is substantially shorter than the Hebrew, omitting the clauses about being comforted when seeing the survivors' ways and deeds; in v. 22, Greek exagousin ("lead out") is also active rather than passive.
notes.15:4: Greek parex ("Apart from that") stands where the Hebrew has "behold," and "the yearly pruning from it" (ten kat' eniauton katharsin ap' autes) reflects a different reading of the Hebrew phrase "both its ends."
notes.15:5: Greek me hoti ("how much less") introduces the a fortiori rhetorical question following the negative first clause.
notes.15:7: Greek exeleusontai ("they will come out") is future rather than past, and epignosontai ("they will know") is third person plural rather than second person.
notes.16:4: Greek 'ouk edesas tous mastous sou' ("you did not bind your breasts") reflects a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Masoretic Hebrew has "your umbilical cord was not cut."
notes.16:7: Greek 'eis poleis poleon' ("into cities of cities") reflects a Septuagint reading of Hebrew 'cities' where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "ornament of ornaments."
notes.16:8: Greek 'kairos katalyonton' literally means "a time of those who lodge" (or "of those who unbind/dissolve"), a difficult Septuagint rendering where the Masoretic Hebrew has "a time of love."
notes.16:27: Greek 'ean de' ("But if"), 'allophylon' ("foreigners," the standard Septuagint rendering for "Philistines"), and 'tas ekklinousas se' ("who turn you aside") reflect distinctive Septuagint readings; 'esebesas' ("You acted impiously") begins the clause completed in verse 28.
notes.16:30: Greek 'ti diatho ten thygatera sou' ("How should I deal with your daughter") and 'trissos en tais thygatrasin sou' ("threefold among your daughters") reflect distinctive Septuagint readings differing markedly from the Masoretic Hebrew.
notes.16:36: Greek 'ton chalkon sou' ("your bronze," also used for copper money) reflects the Septuagint reading of Hebrew 'nehoshet' as bronze/money rather than "lust/nakedness"; Greek 'enthymemata' ("devices/thoughts") regularly renders Hebrew "idols" in Ezekiel.
notes.16:42: Greek 'ou me merimneso' ("I will by no means be anxious") is a distinctive Septuagint rendering where the Masoretic Hebrew has "I will no longer be angry."
notes.16:53: Greek 'apostrepso tas apostrophas' ("I will turn back their turnings away") renders the Hebrew idiom for restoring fortunes or captivity with a literal Greek cognate phrase.
notes.16:59: Greek 'tauta' ("these things") reflects a Septuagint reading of the Hebrew consonants as "these" rather than the Masoretic vocalization "oath."
notes.16:61: Greek 'eis oikodomen' ("for building up") reflects a Septuagint reading of the Hebrew consonants from the root "to build" rather than the Masoretic vocalization "for daughters."
notes.17:3: The Greek reads "full of claws" (pleres onychon, cf. v. 7) and "who has the design to enter Lebanon" (hos echei to hegema eiselthein), diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("full of plumage of varied colors came to Lebanon").
notes.17:12: The Septuagint casts the interpretation across vv. 12-15 in the future tense ("When the king of Babylon comes... he will take"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text narrates it in the past tense.
notes.17:16: The Greek contains a nominative anacoluthon (literally "in the place, the king who made him king"), rendered here as "in the place of the king who made him king," and reads "My curse" and "My covenant" rather than referring to the king's oath and covenant as in the Hebrew.
notes.17:18: The Greek critical text reads the first-person singular perfect verb dedoka ("I have given his hand") rather than the third-person singular ("he gave his hand") found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:23: The Greek kremaso auton ("I will hang it," lit. "him") reflects reading Hebrew talul ("lofty") as a form of the verb "to hang," and the closing clause reads "its branches will be restored" rather than describing birds dwelling in its branches.
notes.18:6: Here and in v. 15 the Greek renders Hebrew "idols" with ta enthymemata ("the devices" or "contrivances"), distinct from ta eidola ("the idols") in v. 12.
notes.18:9: "He will surely live" renders the emphatic Greek dative idiom zoe zesetai (literally "with life he will live"), which mirrors the Hebrew infinitive absolute throughout this chapter.
notes.18:11: The Greek reads "he did not walk in the way of his righteous father," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("though he himself did none of these things").
notes.18:32: The Greek text ends the chapter after "says the Lord," without the closing imperative "so turn and live" present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.19:2: The Greek calls the mother a skymnos ("lion cub") rather than "lioness" as in the Hebrew, and reads "she came to be" (egenethe) and "she multiplied her cubs."
notes.19:4: Here and in v. 8 the Greek translates Hebrew shachat ("pit") by its other sense diaphthora ("destruction"), and renders "with hooks" as en kemo ("in a muzzle," cf. v. 9).
notes.19:7: The Greek reads kai enemeto to thrasei autou ("and he fed in his boldness"), diverging notably from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("and he knew [or ravaged] their widows [or citadels]").
notes.19:10: The Greek reads "and like a blossom on a pomegranate tree" (kai hos anthos en roa), diverging from the difficult Hebrew reading usually rendered "in your blood" or "in your likeness."
notes.19:14: Reading Hebrew shevet limshol ("a scepter for ruling") as phyle eis parabolen ("a tribe for a parable"), the Greek concludes with "a tribe is for a parable of lamentation, and it will be for a lamentation."
notes.20:4: Greek ei ekdikeso autous ekdikesei continues the negative oath formula from v. 3 ("As I live, I will certainly not...") with a shift to the third person ("them") and a cognate dative ("avenge them with vengeance"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads a second-person question ("Will you judge them?").
notes.20:6: Greek kerion ("honeycomb") is a distinctive Septuagint reading (also in v. 15) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "glory/ornament," and Greek hetoimasa reads "prepared" rather than "searched out."
notes.20:26: The Greek uses a future verb ("I will defile") and makes God the subject of diaporeuesthai ("when I pass through everything that opens a womb"), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's past tense and causal reference to passing firstborn through fire, and omits the closing recognition clause.
notes.20:29: Habana (Greek habana/Habana) is a Septuagint transliteration of the Hebrew habbamah ("the high place"), kept here as an LXX-distinct proper name.
notes.20:38: Greek kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord") is a doubled divine title, recurring in vv. 39 and 40; the Hebrew MT has Adonai YHWH in vv. 39-40 but only YHWH here.
notes.21:2: LXX reads "Dagon" (Δαγών) where Hebrew MT has "south" (darom), and "leading" (ἡγούμενον) modifying "forest" where MT has "of the field." LXX also begins chapter 21 here (corresponding to MT 20:45-21:32).
notes.21:3: The Greek doubles the divine title (κύριος Κύριος, "the Lord, the Lord") to represent Hebrew Adonai YHWH. Greek ἀπηλιώτου literally means "east" (also in 21:9), where Hebrew MT reads "south."
notes.21:8: LXX reads "the unrighteous and the lawless" (ἄδικον καὶ ἄνομον, also in 21:9) rather than MT's "the righteous and the wicked." Greek uses ἐγχειρίδιον ("dagger") in vv. 8-10 before switching to ῥομφαία ("sword") in vv. 14-33.
notes.21:18: Verses 17-20 preserve notably difficult LXX readings, including "they will sojourn" and "clap upon your hand" (vs. MT "thigh") in v. 17, "it has been justified; and should a tribe be rejected?" in v. 18, and the negation "so that the heart may not be broken" in v. 20.
notes.21:25: In v. 26, LXX reads "ancient road" and singular "rod" (vs. MT "arrows"), and in vv. 31-32 reads indicative verbs ("you have taken off... put on") and "injustice" (vs. MT "ruin").
notes.22:3: Greek ἐνθυμήματα ("devices" or "schemes," also in 22:4) is LXX Ezekiel's characteristic rendering of Hebrew gillulim ("idols").
notes.22:16: LXX reads a first-person active verb κατακληρονομήσω ("I will take possession"), diverging from MT's "you will be profaned" (or "take possession for yourself").
notes.22:25: LXX reads "whose leaders" (ἧς οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι), diverging from MT's "a conspiracy of her prophets," and in v. 24 has "not watered" (οὐ βρεχομένη) where MT reads "not cleansed."
notes.22:29: LXX places "the people of the land" (λαὸν τῆς γῆς) in the accusative as the victims being extorted by the ruling classes, rather than as the grammatical subject as in MT. In v. 28, LXX reads "will fall" (πεσοῦνται) where MT has "whitewash."
notes.23:5: Greek epitithemai epi (literally "set/throw oneself upon") is used throughout this chapter (vv. 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, 20; cognate noun epithesis in v. 11) for passionate or lustful pursuit.
notes.23:7: Greek enthymemata ("devices" or "thoughts," also in vv. 30, 37, 49) is the Septuagint's characteristic rendering in Ezekiel for the Hebrew term for idols, distinct from eidola ("idols") in v. 39. The Greek also reads the singular pronoun "her devices" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "their idols."
notes.23:15: Greek trissos ("threefold," also in v. 23) reflects the Septuagint's rendering of the Hebrew term for military officers (shalishim) by its connection to the number three. The Greek text also preserves the singular pronoun in "his homeland."
notes.23:23: "Phakouk, Soue, and Hychoue" reflect the Greek proper-name forms Phakouk, Soue, and Hychoue, corresponding to Pekod, Shoa, and Koa in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:34: The Greek text reads "and I will turn away her festivals and her new moons," differing substantially from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which speaks of draining the cup, gnawing its sherds, and tearing the breasts.
notes.24:9: The Greek reads "the people" (ton laon), likely an early scribal shift from "the firebrand" (ton dalon), whereas the Hebrew MT reads "the pile."
notes.24:12: The Greek reads "will be put to shame" (kataischynthesetai), reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants rendered "in the fire" in the MT.
notes.24:17: The Greek ("a groaning of blood, of loins, of mourning you will be; your hair will not be braided upon you... nor be comforted by their lips") diverges markedly from the Hebrew MT ("groan silently; make no mourning for the dead; bind on your turban... do not cover your mustache"). Greek omits a repeated verb before "and your sandals on your feet," which in context (compare v. 23) stands outside the preceding negation.
notes.24:18: The Greek omits the report of Ezekiel's wife's death found in the Hebrew MT ("and in the evening my wife died"), reading instead "just as He commanded me in the evening."
notes.24:24: The Greek reads second-person plural "you have done" (epoiesate), where the Hebrew MT has third-person singular "he has done."
notes.25:4: Greek "Kedem" transliterates the Hebrew word for "East" ("people of the East"), here and in v. 10; "your fatness" (pioteta) reflects a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants for "your milk."
notes.25:9: Greek "the house of Thasimouth, of the ascent of a coastal city" corresponds to the three Moabite cities named in the Hebrew MT (Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim).
notes.25:12: Greek "Idumea" (vv. 12-14) corresponds to Hebrew "Edom"; in v. 13 Greek "those pursued from Teman" differs from the Hebrew MT ("from Teman even to Dedan").
notes.25:15: Greek "the foreigners" (hoi allophyloi, vv. 15-16) is the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines, and in v. 16 Greek renders Hebrew "Cherethites" as "Cretans" (Kretas).
notes.26:2: Throughout this chapter the Greek uses the transliterated form "Sor" for Tyre; here it also reads "the nations have perished... she who was full has been laid desolate" where the Hebrew MT has "the gate of the peoples... I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste."
notes.26:10: Greek "from a plain" (ek pediou) reflects a different reading of the Hebrew root translated "a breached city" in the MT.
notes.26:12: The Greek uses third-person singular verbs throughout vv. 12-13 ("he will plunder... he will put an end to") and reads "your sea" (MT: "the waters"), whereas the Hebrew MT has third-person plural verbs in v. 12 and first-person singular in v. 13.
notes.26:15: Greek reads kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord") here and in vv. 19 and 21, reflecting the doubled divine title in the Hebrew; "when a sword is drawn" also differs from the MT ("when slaughter is made").
notes.26:20: Greek "nor rise up upon the land of life" diverges from the Hebrew MT ("and I will set glory in the land of the living"); v. 21 likewise reads "a destruction" where the MT has "terrors" and lacks the final MT clause.
notes.27:4: Throughout chapter 27 the Greek calls Tyre Sor (transliterating Hebrew Tsor, versus Tyros in chapter 28). Here the Greek also reads the proper name Beelim and "your sons," whereas the Hebrew MT has "your borders" and "your builders."
notes.27:9: Greek uses the classical name Byblos for Hebrew Gebal, reads "strengthening your counsel" (MT "caulking your seams"), and renders Hebrew ma'arab ("merchandise") as "to the west of the west" (epi dysmas dysmon).
notes.27:12: Greek renders Hebrew Tarshish as Carthaginians here (contrast Tarshish in v. 16); likewise in v. 13 Greek renders Hebrew Javan, Tubal, and Meshech as "Greece, and the whole world, and the bordering regions," and in v. 15 reads Rhodians where the MT has Dedan.
notes.27:16: Greek reads "human beings," Tarshish, and the proper names Lamoth and Chorchor (where the MT has Aram/Edom, linen, coral, and rubies), and renders Hebrew ma'arab as "mixed wares" (symmiktos, vv. 16-34). Similarly, Greek reads Miletus in v. 18, Asel and "a wheel" (trochias) in v. 19, and Charman in v. 24 (MT Chilmad).
notes.27:32: Verse 31 of the Hebrew MT is absent from this Greek text, and here Greek reads "their sons" and omits the opening question of the lament ("Who is like Tyre?").
notes.28:2: Greek theos without the article is rendered "a god" here and in vv. 6, 9 to match the contrast with "a man," though it can also be translated "God." In v. 3 Greek asks two rhetorical questions rather than making the declarative statements of the Hebrew MT.
notes.28:12: Greek reads the double divine title kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord," also v. 25) and addresses "the ruler of Tyre" (as in v. 2), where the MT here has "king."
